stakeholderMapping.approach: Map every project's stakeholders within the first discovery call. Identify who decides, who influences, who implements, and who can block.

roles.decider: Has final budget authority. Often CEO/MD or CFO. Must be engaged before final proposal is presented.
roles.influencer: Shapes the brief and evaluates options but doesn't hold budget authority. Often Office Manager, EA, or designer.
roles.implementer: Coordinates day-to-day: installation access, IT scheduling, building management liaison. Office Manager or Facilities Manager.
roles.blocker: Person who can kill the deal — often CFO if not engaged early, or IT Manager if AV/power requirements aren't addressed.

sellingToMultipleStakeholders.CEO: Lead with vision and brand. Show an aspirational environment. Reference comparable companies. Use GOJO Vol 2 and premium product imagery.
sellingToMultipleStakeholders.CFO: Lead with certainty and value. TCO argument. 6-year warranty savings. Itemised quote. Milestone payment option. ISO certifications as quality assurance.
sellingToMultipleStakeholders.OfficeManager: Lead with service and certainty. Clear timeline. Responsive communication. Equip them to present internally. Make them look good.
sellingToMultipleStakeholders.ITManager: Lead with technical compatibility. Confirm cable management, AV integration requirements, power routing. Coordinate delivery after IT cabling.
sellingToMultipleStakeholders.Architect_Designer: Lead with design language, product aesthetics, material quality. Position GOJO Vol 2 heritage narrative. Provide full spec sheets and catalogue imagery.

powerDynamics.identifyingThePowerBroker: The person who controls next steps is not always the most senior. An EA who books meetings and coordinates the evaluation has structural power — invest in this relationship.
powerDynamics.navigationRule: Never go around an influencer to reach a decider without flagging it. It will be noticed and will damage the relationship with the influencer who could block the deal.
powerDynamics.multiThreading: In deals above $100k, aim to have direct contact with at least 2 stakeholders. If your champion leaves or goes on leave, you still have a relationship in the account.

groupDecisionDynamics.committeePresentation: When presenting to a group, address the decider but acknowledge the room. 'For your CFO, the warranty structure means...' / 'For your team, the design means...'
groupDecisionDynamics.dissenterHandling: Identify any dissenter in the room early. Their objection is the one that can kill the deal. Address it directly and specifically.
groupDecisionDynamics.consensusBuilding: In B2B committee decisions, unanimous enthusiasm is rare. Aim for: decider enthusiastic + influencer satisfied + blockers neutralised.
